title: Value of client_secret in a HubSpot OAuth token request
summary: A synthetic value of the client_secret field beside client_id in a curl --data client-credentials request, a raw HTTP authorization-code form body and an introspection request body.
rationale: HubSpot documents the app client secret as the client_secret field of the URL-form encoded body of requests to the OAuth token endpoint, and says that keeping parameters in the body keeps values such as client_id and client_secret out of server logs. The page states no prefix, alphabet or width, so the value is flagged because of the field it sits in, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only. The client_id beside it is public configuration, and an HMAC request signature derived from the secret is not the secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value of an exact client_secret field of an OAuth token request is treated as a credential whatever its shape and covered whole. HubSpot documents the client_secret form field of the token endpoint (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic attribution are the project's decisions. No prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: client_secret | String | The app’s client secret.

To generate a client credentials access token, make a URL-form encoded POST request to /oauth/2026-09/token with grant_type=client_credentials. (parameters: grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
